story: Predicting the digit right after a London postcode letter prefix (WC2, SW1, N1) or a map-grid letter (C5, E7) at the end of an address or index line.
Predicting the first lowercase chunk of a website name immediately after 'www.', echoing the venue that was just named.
Predicting the full stop that ends a flowing descriptive sentence; the newline target is dropped because newlines after bullet-list lines caused almost all the false alarms.
Predicting the pound sign before a price, or a famous English name like 'England' or 'Thames'; ' London' is dropped because it mostly fired on non-member 'Tower of London' repeats.
Predicting a hyphen wherever it joins a compound, range, or time span (snow-capped, 45-minute, 9am-6pm), not only after ordinals like '19th' which were mostly non-members.
Predicting the newline right after an all-caps venue-category tag (MUSEUM, CLUB, VENUE, HOTEL, CHURCH, CEMETERY, HARBOUR...) or a 'Getting There & Away' heading in the listing layout.

Predicting the comma after a one-word item in a comma-separated list, where the token two back is also a comma (film, music, theatre / Cambridge, Hull, ...), excluding commas after multi-word phrases.
Completing the second piece of a multi-token British place name (King's, St James's, Waterloo, Eastbourne, Southbank, Pentonville, Covent, Kew).
